properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-21, before any flo2-driven change is made. Nothing here is intent and nothing is settled.

HIS CONCERN, in his words: "my concern is that by making the changes to reflow2 required by flo2, that it wouldn't be able to support its original use case (which is how we are currently using it now). that's why I was thinking we need to consider this early because I would hate to break the current use case because we made a whole bunch of changes to make reflow2 work for flo2."

⭐ IDEA A — THE LOCAL CASE IS DEFENDED BY INTENT BUT NOT BY A GUARD, AND THAT IS THE GAP. Three things already stand between flo2's work and a broken local path: `req:persistence` (accepted — the design lives at ./.reflow2/graph inside the repo, travelling with it), `req:invocation` (accepted — an MCP server over stdio), and `dec:one-process-many-stores`' own instruction that "the overwhelmingly common case is one project, one directory, --graph-path, and it must keep working exactly as it does", with the framing "single-graph mode is multi-graph mode with a registry of one, pre-populated at startup and with selection defaulted — NOT a second code path". That framing is the right shape and it is a DESIGN PRINCIPLE, not a check. Nothing today fails when it stops being true. The cheap answer to a regression worry is a guard, not a promise.

⭐ IDEA B — HIS STATED SCALE MAY EXCEED WHAT THE ACCEPTED DECISION COVERS. flo2 is a web app at flo2.io, collaborative (many people on the SAME project at once) and expecting on the order of 10,000 simultaneously logged-in users across DIFFERENT projects. `dec:one-process-many-stores` accepts N open RocksDB stores in one process, each carrying its own block cache, file handles and tantivy index, and names resource exhaustion as an accepted risk requiring "a cap on simultaneously open graphs, with a clear error at the cap rather than silent thrashing". 10,000 open stores in one process is not that shape. At that number the answer is partitioning across many processes — which is item #8, blast radius, which flo2's own tracker says to decide BEFORE designing the registry because "retrofitting it onto a registry designed for one process is a rewrite of the piece everything else is gated on". The decision was accepted without a number attached; the number changes which question is being answered.

⭐ IDEA C — AND THAT MAY CUT THE OTHER WAY, WHICH IS THE HOPEFUL VERSION. A sharded shape — many processes, each holding few graphs — is CLOSER to today's local behaviour than one fat process holding everything. If the answer at 10k is partitioning, the invasiveness to the local path may go DOWN rather than up, because each process keeps roughly the shape it has now. Recorded as a possibility, not a claim; nobody has designed it.

⭐ IDEA D — THE COLLABORATIVE AXIS MAY ALREADY BE MET AND IS WORTH NOT REBUILDING. "Many people on the same project at once" is `req:sessions-share-a-graph` (accepted) delivered by `cap:shared-sessions` (VERIFIED — "several sessions work one design at once, through one server"). Single-writer is not relaxed by any of this: one process holds the lock, many sessions speak to it. So flo2's collaboration requirement may need nothing new, and the genuinely unbuilt axis is the many-PROJECTS one.

WHAT IS NOT IN DOUBT, so it does not get re-litigated here: whether flo2 gets its own fork. `dec:one-process-many-stores` answers that — one reflow2, N single-writer stores, the directory stays the unit of a design — and it explicitly rejected many-designs-in-one-store. The open questions above are about SHAPE and PROOF, not about forking.

🛑 A SEPARATE DEFECT NOTICED WHILE READING, not part of this question: `dec:one-process-many-stores` carries `status: accepted` and a name beginning "ACCEPTED 2026-08-06 (conditional)", while its own body opens "PROPOSED, NOT SETTLED." The status moved and the text did not. A reader can honestly conclude either. Left alone — whether it is settled is Anthony's to say.

DISTINCT FROM the three nodes the guard surfaced. `dec:one-process-many-stores` decides the SHAPE of hosting and assumes it is worth doing; this asks what it COSTS the existing case and whether a stated scale still fits. `req:many-people-and-many-projects-compose` requires the two axes to hold together; this asks what would PROVE a third thing — the local path — still holds while they do. `dec:the-registry-root-is-the-tenant-boundary` settles where the tenant line falls inside the registry; this asks whether a registry of that shape survives 10k.
properties.name: OPEN — what would PROVE that building for flo2 has not broken the local single-project case, and does 10k tenants even fit the accepted shape?
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill: recorded as ideas so nothing is lost and nothing is claimed as intent. Anthony raised it deliberately EARLY — before the flo2-driven changes are made rather than after — which is the whole point of recording it now.

The four ideas are kept apart because they have different answers: A wants a check written, B wants a number decided, C is a possibility nobody has explored, and D may need nothing at all. Collapsing them into one node would make it answerable only in halves.
